messages.subject_clean: Meet and Analyze Data, Wed Apr 3rd 3-5 PM - Bennett Conference Room CCAH
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

we will be having a Meet and Analyze Data session from 3:00pm-5:00pm
today (04/03),
in the Bennett Conference Room at the Center for Companion Animal Health
(http://campusmap.ucdavis.edu/?b=33).
Hope to see you there!

This is the last session of the quarter, we will not be meeting next
week (Spring break).

--

If you think you are going to join us, please let us know --

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeUW5QS55uDwDpusGYerY542D_tQubkmPMtUKlGdbmoSWfSSQ/viewform

--

Meet and Analyze Data (MAD) is a forum to bring your biological big
data and discuss high level concept problems (what is metagenome
assembly?) and low level coding problems (what does this error message
even mean?!) and everything in between. There is no scheduled or
specific activity: people show up with questions about how to analyze
their data, or maybe they are willing to help others. We typically get
questions about experimental design for
transcriptomic/metagenomic/genomic projects, or how to install
software, or how to run their analysis on clusters or the cloud.

Cheers,
Luiz Irber

messages.subject: [dsiaffiliates] Sacramento Women in Data; Next event April 17th 7-9 PM at the Urban Hive
messages.subject_clean: [dsiaffiliates] Sacramento Women in Data; Next event April 17th 7-9 PM at the Urban Hive
messages.body_plain:
For all interested,

Women in Data (WID) in Sacramento is putting on several exciting and useful events. The next event will be on April 17th from 7-9 PM at the Urban Hive in Sacramento (1601 Alhambra Blvd #100, Sacramento, CA). There will be lightning talks on visualizing large datasets with Elasticsearch and Kibana, rapid prototyping of data UIs, a few basics of graphing in R using ggplot2, a group exercise in finding open data sources, and a networking session. If planning on attending, RSVP on meetup:
https://www.meetup.com/Sacramento-Women-in-Data/events/260166687/

If not interested in the above topics, then check on the meetup page later. WID covers many areas accessible for a broad range of expertise (e.g.:  what different data positions are like, how and when to use different programming languages or data management tools, how to find and work with data in training workshops, etc...). WID is also an excellent networking opportunity to meet people that work in data in Sacramento. Men and anyone from non-binary gender identities are also definitely welcome to WID events! Also feel free to contact me with questions.

Women in Data (WID) is a national non-profit organization aimed at increasing diversity in data careers. Click here  <https://widusa.com/about>to check out more on Women in Data.

Best,
Hanna Kahl
Chapter Lead - Women in Data

messages.subject: Sudden packages not loading/unable to locate
messages.subject_clean: Sudden packages not loading/unable to locate
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Yesterday I started a new script and tried to load all my packages in the working environment (I have a standard set, see code below).

options(repos = c(CRAN = 'https://cloud.r-project.org'))
list_of_packages <- c('tidyverse', 'reticulate','tidyr',
                      'tibble','packrat','plyr','broom',
                      'data.table','colorspace','reshape2','ggplot2',
                      'plotly','sm','ggpubr','gridExtra','devtools', 'xlsx',
                      'extrafont', 'ggsignif','IDPmisc')
new_packges_to_load <- list_of_packages[!(list_of_packages %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
if(length(new_packges_to_load)) install.packages(new_packges_to_load, dependencies = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
lapply(list_of_packages, function(x)require(x, character.only = T, quietly = T))

This normally works well, however, yesterday I had some weird errors come up that I am quite concerned with.

Error in gzfile(file, mode) : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning message:
In gzfile(file, mode) :
  cannot open compressed file 'C:\Users\DANIEL~1.STE\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpWAuLWC/libloc_185_b6156d26.rds', probable reason 'No such file or directory'

I initially thought it was something due to my internet, but it's working fine and I cannot load in any packages I know I already installed as R studio can no longer locate them. I also suddenly can't redownload the package either as it can't be found.

Has anyone ever ran into anything like this and knows a solution to fix it? Because I'm dead in the water with ideas.

Thank you so much in advance!!
Dani Stevens
--
Danielle (Dani) Stevens
Ph.D. Student
Integrative Genetics & Genomics | UC Davis

messages.subject_clean: [D-RUG]: Sudden packages not loading/unable to locate
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dani,

I don’t have a solid answer, but a couple diagnostic thoughts:

1.  Did you recently update R?
2.  Do you know exactly which step is failing, and exactly which packages are involved in that failure?
3.  What happens if you don’t set the repos option?

As an aside, tidyverse already loads tidyr, tibble, and ggplot2 (and possibly a few other packages in your list), and loading all three of dplyr (via tidyverse), plyr, and data.table will create a bunch of namespace conflicts that can make your life more complicated (e.g., both dplyr and data.table have a between() function).  So I wouldn’t necessarily automatically load everything in your list.

Cheers,
Dan
----
Daniel J. Hicks
Postdoctoral Researcher
Data Science Initiative
University of California, Davis

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Neuralnetwork and Keras issues
messages.body_plain:
The sessionInfo() part is just to let us all know what your computing
environment is.  You might, for instance, be using an obsolete version
of R or of some relevant package.  That doesn't seem to be the case
here, but if it were, the easy fix would be to tell you to update R
and/or the package.

Regarding spaces in file names, let me give an example.  My base
directory for my R documents is:

    /home/mike/Documents/R

I *could* make a different directory, call it:

   My Documents

such that my base directory for R would be:

    /home/mike/My Documents/R

That path name has a space in it (between "My" and "Documents").
That's perfectly OK from the point of view of the file system in
general, but it may be that a given R package would parse that as:

    /home/mike/My

plus some "garbage" at the end:

     Documents/R

I'm not saying that *is* your problem, just that the error message you
posted resembles that kind of message.

messages.subject: #maptimeDavis NDVI Time Series Data in R
messages.subject_clean: #maptimeDavis NDVI Time Series Data in R
messages.body_plain:
Workshop: NDVI Time Series Data in R

Tuesday, 4/23 1:00-3:00 in the DSI Classroom – room 360 Shields Library with speakers Mahesh Maskey & Kristen Shapiro

Learn how to use R over time and have a great time at this workshop. NDVI  (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) information is very useful in various field of studies like agriculture, crop yield, types of vegetation, plant phenology, climate change, seasonal change and beyond. This workshop outlines a method to extract NDVI from Landsat remotely sensed images over different periods of year in R. In addition, participants will explore widely used R-functions in visualizing both temporal and spatial dynamics of NDVI.

Objectives

- to learn how to deal with remotely sensed images to extract physical quantities like NDVI

- to visualize raster image and relevant statistics

- to perform raster calculations

- to extract NDVI time series from different periods of observation

- to visualize spatial dynamics

Please bring a laptop with R or R Studio installed.  More information and link to register:  https://spatial.ucdavis.edu/2019/04/16/maptimedavis-ndvi-time-series-data-in-r/

Best,

Michele

messages.subject: p-median Location Allocation Modelling
messages.body_plain:
Hi ya'll,
I am currently working on a project that attempts to find the optimal locations for biogas generators in Los Angeles county. I have already worked out a number of potential locations, I just need to find which set of locations are optimal based on reducing the cost of transporting fuel (in this case food waste) to the generator.

I've narrowed my problem down to a variation of the p-median model. The classic example of these problems is finding locations for n firehouses so all residents in a city are within x minutes of a station. I'm attaching a book chapter that explains it in more detail if you're interested.

Does anybody have experience (or know someone with experience) with this type of location-allocation modelling? An ideal situation is there is a package that already exists, but I think I could make the R code myself if someone could explain math to me (the attached book chapter explains it and even provides some pseudocode, but its still at a level slightly higher than my current math comprehension)

Any kind of help/direction/sympathy is highly appreciated!
Thank you,
Lauren Mabe

Hi all,

we will be having a Meet and Analyze Data session from 3:00pm-5:00pm

If you think you are going to join us, please let us know --

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeUW5QS55uDwDpusGYerY542D_tQubkmPMtUKlGdbmoSWfSSQ/viewform

--

Meet and Analyze Data (MAD) is a forum to bring your biological big
data and discuss high level concept problems (what is metagenome
assembly?) and low level coding problems (what does this error message
even mean?!) and everything in between. There is no scheduled or
specific activity: people show up with questions about how to analyze
their data, or maybe they are willing to help others. We typically get
questions about experimental design for
transcriptomic/metagenomic/genomic projects, or how to install
software, or how to run their analysis on clusters or the cloud.

Cheers,
Luiz Irber
